findings.reason: §17 must either move `landed_section_ids` into `_plan_html.py` as the one predicate (retiring the `_store` name) or justify why a parallel public predicate cannot replace it, which it does not.
findings.text: §17 (§16 depends on it) introduces a second public recogniser of a landed card, the predicate "the parser module exposes beside the identity function", while `reckon/_store.py:1034 landed_section_ids` is already the exported recogniser of exactly that (a heading whose nearest enclosing `<section>` is a `section-landed` card), deliberately established as "the one definition" by §14; §17 demotes it to a reader of the new predicate, so the package carries two public definitions answering one question and the writer/reader pair §17 says must "share one definition of a card" has two

findings.reason: a forwarded alias with two years of would-be callers is the surface §17 exists to remove, so the plan should delete the alias rather than keep a wrapper it never justifies.
findings.text: after §17, `landed_section_ids` adds no behaviour the new predicate on `reckon/_plan_html.py` lacks; it forwards to it, and the section gives no reason the two callers that cross the boundary (`plan_review.py` and `doccheck.py`) cannot import the predicate from its one home

findings.reason: the interface-budget rule requires the section to name what it retires or merges, and the obvious merge — `landed_section_ids` onto the new predicate — is neither named nor declined, so the section's own accounting is incomplete.
findings.text: §17's interface accounting ("two public definitions are added on `reckon/_plan_html.py` … the retired walks were private, so the net is two") counts the card predicate as pure addition and names no retirement or merge, yet `landed_section_ids` (reckon/_store.py:1034) is a public definition in the same family answering the same question; taken with §16's one and §18's one the family grows by four, where consolidating the recogniser would grow it by three, and the section states no reason nothing can be retired

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the per-section fingerprint machinery is hidden behind one small interface: `plan_fingerprint` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:368) keeps returning a single digest, with `_section_digests`, the coverage predicate and the third recognised form all module-private on plan_review.py, and §17 exposes one public reader `plan_headings` over a private parser.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §17's new public card predicate duplicates `landed_section_ids` (reckon/_store.py:1034), the exported card recogniser §14 established as "the one definition", and neither §17 nor §16's interface accounting names that owner to move or extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 adds two public definitions on `reckon/_plan_html.py` (`plan_headings` and the card predicate) and retires only private walks, so it neither names `landed_section_ids` as retired or merged into the new predicate nor states why it cannot be, while §16 and §18 add one each.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the unlanded design (§16–§18) names and reuses the mechanisms it would otherwise rebuild: §17 extends `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` / `structured_section_spans` (reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94) and the `reckon/interface_counts.py` AST census rather than adding a scanner, and §18 hoists the existing `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:7236) rather than forking it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §17 keeps `reckon/_store.py:1034 landed_section_ids` as "a reader of the public reader's output" while adding the new card predicate on `_plan_html.py`, a thin forwarding layer over the predicate with no stated reason a caller cannot use the predicate directly.
